He was instrumental in getting the inner reservation for Arunthathiyar community. When our Party President, Thalapathy M.K. Stalin was the Minister for Local Bodies and Administration, he was instrumental in filling-up all the vacancies which were reserved for the inner reservation of the Arunthathiyar community, particularly for the women vacancies in an effective way. 

Dr. Kalaignar was the first one to propose and implement reservation for destitute women, physically challenged persons, and for the transgenders. He brought the 33 per cent reservation for women in local bodies, and 30 per cent reservation for women in Government jobs. The Tamil Nadu Government during his days and at present, provides 69 per cent reservation, for which the then Chief Minister, Dr. Kalaignar was instrumental. 

Madam, they say that all are equal, but some are more equal than others. In order to have a fair and balanced equality, I urge the Government to bring a reservation Act for OBCs, SCs, and STs and to place it in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution. I am proud to remind here that the Government of Tamil Nadu, headed by Dr. Kalaignar, was the first Government to create a separate Ministry for Backward Classes way back in 1969. 

I wish to bring to the notice of this august House a matter of very urgent importance. The three-member expert committee on Creamy Layer for OBCs is needless and unwarranted since we already have a constitutional body, the National Commission on Backward Classes to look after the OBC’s related issues. 

15.00 hrs

It is sad to note that in that Committee not a single member is from the OBC. To determine a creamy layer on the basis of salaried income only and to remove Groups A and B is unjustifiable and could eliminate the deserving candidates belonging to the OBCs. That is why, our dear Dr. Kalaignar called the creamy layer as the `kirumi’ layer’. `Kirumi’ in Tamil means virus in English. The Government has totally ignored the report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Welfare of OBCs dated 9.3.2019. (…interruptions) Madam, I am the only speaker from my Party. 

Therefore, I urge the Ministry to reject the three-member Expert Committee and advise the National Commission on Backward Classes to look into the issue of various posts in Public Sector Undertakings and on creamy layer. Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere. I wish to record the grave injustice being done to the OBC students in the seat allotments of MBBS and Post-Graduate medical seats under all India quota. Though this issue relates to the Ministry of Health, I want to record this in the discussion under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment since this is a problem related to the implementation of social justice. 

The 27 per cent reservation mandated by the Government for the OBC students has not been implemented by the Medical Council of India in all India quota seats. This has to be taken note of and the Health Ministry has to take a decision to extend 27 per cent reservation to OBC students and should file in a reply in the Supreme Court. I have got the data about the lack of funds allotted to the post-matric scholarship as well as pre-matric scholarship to all the students. It has to be increased. The inadequate budget allocation under these schemes is because of the gap between the funds decided by the Ministry of Social Justice and those approved by the Ministry of Finance. It should be bridged. 

Madam, justice delayed is justice denied. The implementation of reservation for SCs, STs and OBCs in higher educational institutions, funded by the Centre, was delayed by 15 years after the announcement while the same for EWS was done within a month of its announcement. This disparity should be set right. Again, the Ministry of Social Justice has created Dr. Ambedkar Foundation and allotted funds. We are happy and it is a welcome move. Similarly, the Government has to create Thanthai Periyar Foundation for furthering the ideology and message of Thanthai Periyar. 

Madam, coming to the issue of empowerment of women, we are now in the millennial era talking about empowerment but way back in the 4th century BC when Aristotle was lecturing to his students that women were subjective to men and that men were rulers and women were subjects, it was Augustine, a woman who disguised herself as a man and became the world’s first women doctor. Who was Plato’s teacher? It was Miletus Aspasia who was a woman, celebrated as the first lady of Athens. But here, in this, even after the Government having declared the year 2001 as the year of Women Empowerment, we are still fighting for 33 per cent reservation for women. Is it not a shame? I wish to place on record that reservation is our birth right. It is neither a concession nor any alms given as mercy to us. We want minimum, not maximum, 50 per cent reservation and the Government should take steps to implement the 33 per cent reservation. Dr. Kalaignar implemented 50 per cent reservation for women in urban and local bodies. So, Tamil Nadu is the first State to do so in the whole country. 

Madam, right is its own defence. I wish to urge the Ministry, through you, to allot more funds for the persons with disabilities. There are 70 million people with disabilities and are physically challenged. The funds allocated is only Rs. 330 crore. The Government should increase the allocation. Also, the funds for the Deen Dayal Disabled Rehabilitation Programme should be increased. Under the Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana, I have adopted a village by name Sitalapakkam. I urge the Central Ministry to put pressure on the State Government because the Government of Tamil Nadu has sent back the Nirbhaya Fund without properly utilising the whole amount. 

It is a shame on the AIADMK Government for not having fully utilized the funds. 

I would like to conclude my speech again with Brecht who said: 

“Those who take the meat from the table teach contentment.

Those for whom the taxes are destined demand sacrifice. 

Those who eat their fill speak to the hungry of wonderful times to come.

Those who lead the country into the abyss call ruling too difficult for ordinary men.”

With these words, I conclude my speech. 

SHRIMATI PRATIMA MONDAL (JAYNAGAR): Madam, I rise to speak on the Demands for Grants pertaining to Social Justice and Empowerment for the year 2020-21. 

15.06 hrs (Shri Kodikunnil Suresh in the Chair) 

Sir, social justice is a concept of a society in which every human being is treated justly, without discrimination based on financial status, race, gender, ethnicity and caste in the country. Eradication of this discrimination must be accompanied with empowerment which will ensure a healthy society. Need of the hour is to turn this mere concept into a reality. It will be unfair to say that proper steps are not being taken by the Government, but they are not sufficient. Innumerable schemes being formed on paper are not the solution of unjust happenings in the country. 

A key to the solution is proper implementation, just like quality is preferred over quantity. Of all the things that are so crucial not only for India but also for the entire world is women’s participation. Until and unless little girls are educated and provided opportunity to prosper in life, social justice will never be achieved. Social justice is also incomplete till the time when people are identified by their contribution to the society and not by their caste. Justice is nowhere near when manual scavenging is still going on. The day when Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan will be fully accomplished, then only we can say that absolute justice in Indian society is no longer a dream. But till then, social justice and empowerment seem to be an unachievable utopian concept. 

I would like to draw the attention of the House to the incidents which are disturbing for the entire nation. Firstly, according to the information forwarded by the National Dalit Movement for Justice and the International Dalit Solidarity Network to the UN Human Rights Committee in July, 2019, while the reporting of crimes against Dalits and Adivasis has risen over the decades, there has not been an equivalent rise in the rate of disposal of cases by the police and courts under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. Pending cases of crimes against Scheduled Castes have nearly doubled from 8,380 cases to 16,654 cases in a decade. In the case of crimes against Scheduled Tribes, pending cases of investigation have risen by 55 per cent, from 1,679 cases to 2,602 cases, a submission to the UN said. At the same time, it said, in courts, crimes against SCs pending trial rose by 50 per cent over the decade from 85,264 to 1,29,831. In 2016 alone, for which the latest figures were available, 40,801 new crimes against Dalits were registered under the Prevention of Atrocities Act. Less than 15,000 cases completed trial that year. Forget about the empowerment, there is no justice even after so many schemes being taken up by the Government. 

Secondly, a survey conducted by the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation has reported 45,000 manual scavengers in 170 districts across the county. The year 2019 recorded highest number of deaths in the prohibited profession of manual scavenging. There is no reported conviction under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 since its enactment. Yet, the allocation in this year’s Budget, that is, Rs. 110 crore for the Self Employment Scheme for rehabilitation of manual scavengers is equal to that of the last year. 

Thirdly, the Denotified Nomadic and Semi-nomadic Tribes (DNT) are overlooked once again in this year’s budget. The DNTs are a heterogenous group engaged in various occupations such as transport, key-making, salt trading, entertaining acrobats, dancers, snake charmers, jugglers and pastoralists. Well, the problem lies at the root that they are not even accounted for in the census. The development of DNTs across six years shows a slow growth while the budget allocation is slightly increased in 2018-19 from Rs. 6 crore to Rs. 10 crore. It has been stagnant since then. It is significant to note that the actual expenditure for each year has been below the budgetary allocation showing the inability of DNTs to avail of funds and resources meant for them. Most of them are accounted under the SCs and STs but getting a certificate for the same is difficult for them as they are asked for a proof from 1950s. 

I would like to request the hon. Minister through you Sir that the Government must look into this issue as they have an estimated population of ten per cent of the total population of India. Since the constitution of the Renke Commission to the Idate Commission, there has been no improvement in the situation of DNTs.

Fourthly, the tribal communities remain vulnerable to displacement because of mining, dams and other large infrastructure projects. Distressing incidents of bonded labour also came up in 2019. A man named Kashi was rescued along with 27 others including ten children. They belong to the Irula community, a particularly vulnerable tribal group. Due to the unbearably poor condition, they had to borrow petty amounts and non-repayment of those amounts led to this condition. This is nothing less than slavery. Kashi’s case was brought to the notice of the authority by Released Bonded Labour Association but none of the culprits was booked under the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976. The very next day, the rescued group was threatened to join back. This is not the nation we are trying to build. Several loopholes in the system not only favour the offenders but also promote them to commit even more severe crimes. 

Fifthly, the Union Government’s allocation for the inclusion of persons with disabilities through the Department for the empowerment of persons with disabilities remain 0.04 per cent compared to the total expenditure of the Government during the last three financial years. The Budget documents reveal that allocation for Institute for Sign Language, Institute for Research and Technologies for Persons with Disabilities, and assistive devices both ADIP and ALIMCO has been reduced. There is no mention or provision for enhancing services in rural areas. There is only a marginal increment to RCI which is responsible for producing the pool of experts to work with persons with disabilities. The expansion of quality habitation and rehabilitation services in rural areas will never see the light of the day with this marginal increase of Rs. 0.50 crore. Neither the Government lives up to the aspiration of the persons with disabilities nor is there an obligation to consider and fulfil the recommendation of the CRPD Committee that was released in September, 2019. The gaps identified by the NSSO survey released in December, 2019 are also ignored. 

Coming to the immediate steps that the Government should take immediately, firstly, overall, the Demands for Grants for the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities should be increased. Secondly, the Centre’s contribution to pensions of disabled persons must be increased. It continued to remain at a meagre of Rs. 300 for the past several years whereas in the State of West Bengal, the hon. Chief Minister, Mamata Banerjee provides assistance of Rs. 1000 per month through the Manobik Scheme. Disability certificates are being distributed through organising medical camps. 

Number three, the National University for Rehabilitation Sciences and Disability Studies announced in 2015, and the National Institute of Mental Health Rehabilitation promised in 2016, are yet to see the light of the day and demand allocations. 

More funds are to be allocated for proper implementation of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 as the suicide rates in India are continuously rising. More funds and impetus for the field of rare diseases is required immediately. It is also necessary to ensure that the Schemes and Programmes are being implemented properly.

HON. CHAIRPERSON : Please conclude.

SHRIMATI PRATIMA MONDAL : I am concluding in just one minute.

The Government must also fill up the backlog vacancies amounting up to 7,782 for SCs, 6,955 for STs, and 10,859 for OBCs in six departments. The information for other departments is not even available.

I would like to conclude by saying that rising walls to hide poverty and pouring water into the River Yamuna for welcoming dignitaries is a petty and temporary solution. It is equivalent to mocking the people of our country. Small steps which give permanent solution must be opted by the Government. It is also the responsibility of the fellow citizens to discharge their duties humanely. Thank you. 

SHRI ACHYUTANANDA SAMANTA (KANDHAMAL): Hon. Chairperson Sir, at the outset, I would like to express my thanks and gratitude to you for giving me an opportunity to participate in the discussion on the Demands for Grants under the control of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for 2020-21.

First of all, I would like to congratulate the hon. Minister, Shri Thaawar Chand Gehlotji for taking up phenomenal welfare initiatives in a time-bound manner, under the leadership of Shri Narendra Modiji, the hon. Prime Minister of India. I think, he knows poverty, he has lived through it, he knows that there is a lot to be done for the upliftment of the downtrodden sections of the society to whose betterment Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkarji was committed, and he is doing it every single day. He understands it, and is committed to social justice. The time has changed. Whether you are in power or in Opposition, what matters is that one should come for people’s help. His Government is doing the same. 

We strongly appreciate that the Budget, 2020-21 presented by the hon. Finance Minister, Shrimati Nirmala Sitharamanji has given a decisive push to social sector with enhanced allocations for welfare schemes, renewed emphasis on education for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and emphasis on the welfare of vulnerable sections of the society, including senior citizens, transgenders and beggars. 

We definitely laud and appreciate the 14 per cent increase in the Budget allocation for the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. I believe that the biggest increase in scholarship schemes for meritorious students from SCs, STs, and OBCs across the Ministries is a testimony of commitment to social justice. I strongly believe that the difference between insignificance and prominence is the bridge of opportunities. Given opportunities and access, anyone can excel. I once again congratulate the Government for this step. To add to it, we appreciate the vision of the Government that the vibrant India shall be a caring society which shall attend to its weak, old, and vulnerable among its citizens. 

Now, I would like to highlight some points regarding the State of Odisha. Our hon. Chief Minister, Shri Naveen Patnaikji charted Odisha’s remarkable turnaround, which was once India’s most backward State. He still remains, by far, the tallest Leader of the State. He remains unwaveringly focussed on the development of the State, and pursues it with relentless zeal through his social security schemes that bring social justice and empowerment. His motto of being attentive to the requirements of the people by always keeping ears open to their problems and trying to deal with them as effectively as possible, is the reason behind the success of his measures in Odisha. The Schemes like Kalia, Madhubabu Pension Yojana, Mamata Scheme, Biju Pucca Ghar Yojana, Biju Krushak Kalyan Yojana, Mukhyamantri Swasthya Seva Mission, Barista Nagarika Tirtha Yatra Yojana, and Kalinga Sikhya Sathi Yojana cover almost 70 per cent of the 4.5 crore people of the State. It is an example for other States. 

Again, under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, programmes that have seen the highest increase include Pre-Matric Scholarship for Children of Workers involved in Manual Scavenging, Fellowships for OBCs, Overseas Fellowships for OBCs, Renewed Thrust on Fighting Drug Abuse, and Care of Senior Citizens and Rehabilitation of Beggars. A National Action Plan for drug demand reduction with an allocation of Rs. 260 crore has been introduced. This is very important and needed. We deeply appreciate the National Action Plan for Senior Citizens which has also seen an increase of 400 per cent in budget allocation from Rs. 40 crore to Rs. 200 crore.

The Union Budget was woven around three prominent themes – Aspirational India, Economic Development for All, and Building a Caring Society. Achieving any of these would require extraordinary efforts on the social sector front starting with allocating additional resources for health, education, nutrition, employment guarantee, and also social security schemes.

HON. CHAIRPERSON : Please conclude.

SHRI ACHYUTANANDA SAMANTA : Sir, I am the only speaker from my party and I have been told that 10 minutes have been allocated for our party.

HON. CHAIRPERSON: No; your party has been allotted only five minutes. Anyhow, you continue.

SHRI ACHYUTANANDA SAMANTA : Sir, the allocation for the social sector this year once again fails to deliver for the country’s poor and marginalised the way it is supposed to.

Now, I come to some other points which really deserve further attention from the Government. Year after year, the allocated budget for the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme has been recording shortfalls and the Ministry has time and again indicated that this adversely affects the beneficiaries. Even this year, only Rs. 2,987 crore and Rs. 1,415 crore have been allocated for the Scheduled Cases and Other Backward Classes respectively, which is a very small improvement from the Budget Estimates of last year. The Ministry should be allocated substantially more sum so that arrears can be cleared and fresh eligible beneficiaries can be identified under this Scheme.

Sir, it is deeply saddening to know that there are nearly no candidates selected under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme since its inception in 2016. This has also led to under-utilization of the budget under this scheme. So, I urge the Ministry to make additional efforts through advertising or take up an exclusive outreach programme to ensure that more people are made aware of the benefits under this Scheme.

It is a terrible truth that manual scavenging is still existing in this country and news of manual scavenging deaths are reported extremely frequently. This is a social evil that has to be eliminated at the earliest and the Ministry should put in a considerable effort to eradicate this. All agencies and bodies of the Government at all levels at the Centre and States should be informed to make notification to prohibit manual cleaning of manholes and strict penalties should be imposed on any contractor who employs manual cleaners. The amount sanctioned under the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers should be utilised best to rehabilitate these affected people and a one-time cash benefit should be provided to help them start a new life of profession. To eradicate the practice of manual cleaning of sewer systems or septic tanks, allocation of Rs. 10,103 crore to the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for the year 2020-21, as against Rs. 8,885 crore given to it in 2019-20 is extremely important. But how it reaches the beneficiaries is really critical.

The allocation made for SC Boys and Girls Hostels has been extremely low for the past few years and even during this year, there has not been any substantial improvement. In the last few years, approximately 40 hostels have been sanctioned and there is no data as to how many of them are functional. Education is very important and hostels form the backbone of educational accommodation. This allocation does not help the backward youth of the country, and so, I urge that the Ministry may allocate a substantial sum to truly help the beneficiaries belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Classes. Similarly, Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana is a good scheme, but only Rs. 1 crore has been allocated for it.

About persons with disabilities, there is 2.8 crore disabled population in the country, but here also, the allocation is not enough to fully take care of them. 

Lastly, I would like to quote what Martin Luther King said. He said

“Life’s most persistent and urgent question is, “What are you doing for others?”

This Ministry has been taking active steps, but the logistics of how it reaches the beneficiaries is the most important aspect.

With these words, I conclude. Thank you.

* SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SADANAND SULE (BARAMATI): The budgetary allocation to the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment in 2020-2l is Rs. 10,103 crore, which is just a mere 0.3% increment over spending by this department in 2018-19. 

Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, Central Sector Scheme that provides physical aides and Assisted living devices for senior citizens suffering from Age Related Disabilities/infirmities belonging to BPL Category. Under this scheme, just Rs. 1 crore is allocated for spending in 2020-21, compared to Rs.106 crore spent in 2018-19 on physical aides. Through this scheme, many elderly with disabilities from my Baramati constituency benefitted over the years and my constituency Baramati is one of the top performing constituencies in the functioning of this scheme. These assisted devices help the differently abled people to have easy mobility and improve their integration into society. Given the immense benefits of this scheme, I request the Centre to increase the budget allocation for this scheme to at least Rs.150 crores. In the 2020-21 budget, no funds are allocated to schemes and programmes responsible for preventing alcoholism, substance and drug abuse.

Assistance to Voluntary Organisations for Programmes Relating to Aged: The Scheme provides financial assistance upto 90% of the project cost for running and maintaining day-care centres, old age homes, mobile Medicare units etc. Also, for a scheme that subsidises provision of old age homes for elderly, no allocation is made this year, compared to Rs. 100 crore spent in 2019-20.

Budgetary allocation for post-matric scholarship for SC students reduced by almost 50% from Rs.5,928 crore in 2018-19 to Rs.2,941 crore in 2020-21. Total amount of funds spent on educational empowerment of students from Scheduled Castes is reduced by 39% from Rs. 6803 crore in 2018-19 to Rs. 3742 crore in the budgetary allocation for the Department of Empowerment of persons with Disabilities is Rs. 1325 crore in 2020-21.

The budgetary allocation for the Department of Employment of Persons with Disabilities is Rs. 1325 crore in 2020-21: Under the Scheme for implementation of Persons with Disability Act, financial assistance is provided to various bodies set up by the Central Government and State Governments to support activities relating to accessible India campaign and implementation of the Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995, particularly relating to rehabilitation and provision of barrier-free access. The funds allocated under this scheme to make India accessible to differently abled persons is reduced by 20% from Rs. 315 crore in 2019.20 to Rs. 251 crore in 2020-21. Total amount projected to be spent in 2020-21 under National Program for Welfare of Persons with disabilities, reduced to Rs. 655 crore in 2020-21 from Rs.688 crore of budget allocation in previous year.

Regarding allocation to denotified tribes (DNT), while the budget slightly increased in 2018-19 to 10 crore from Rs 6 crore, it has been stagnant since then. It was significant to note that, the actual expenditure for each year has been below the budgetary allocation, showing the inability of DNTs to avail of funds and resources meant for them. Based on the Renke Committee report of 2018, not much has changed with respect to the impoverished status of denotified tribes since the Renke Commission (2008) Report. The 2008 report which submitted its report in 2008, highlighted that 50 per cent of DNTs lacked any kind of documents and 98 per cent were landless. In such a situation while the Government has been on an overdrive in accumulating citizen’s data through Aadhaar and now NPR, these are of no use to those who need proof of their identities the most.

Post matriculation scholarship demands exceed allocations: while there has been an increase in budget allocations for scholarship schemes for meritorious students from SCs, STs and OBCs across ministries indicating the Government’s emphasis on education for vulnerable sections of society, it is still not adequate to meet the current demand.

According to the report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Social Justice and Empowerment for 2019-20, the schemes were already underfunded. For 2019-20, the department had sought Rs 14,871.37 crore but received only Rs 8,885 crore. This “adversely affected the Post Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs and Post Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBCs”, noted the report. It also states: “It is evident that the requirements of this department are much more to provide Scholarships, than allocation actually provided to them.” Just Rs 2,926.82 crore had been allocated to the post-matric scholarship scheme for SCs this year, against a demand of Rs 7,125 crore. Consequently, there was already a shortfall of Rs.4,198.18 crore. There is therefore a more significant allocation that is required to be allocated.

Maharashtra-Disbursement of funds under the Post Matric Scholarship Scheme for students belonging to Scheduled Tribes. In Maharashtra, the State Government is implementing the post matric scheme to provide financial assistance to the Scheduled Tribe students Studying at post-matric or post- Secondary stage, Under the scheme Central and State share is 75:25. For the year 2017-18, anticipated expenditure under the scheme was Rs.22411.94 lakh out of which the Centre is required to provide Rs.16808.95 lakh. A proposal for the disbursal of these funds had been submitted to the Government of India through a state Government letter dated 18 April 2017. The Government of India has only released Rs.3623.75 lakh grant by a letter dated May 2017. However the remaining grant is still pending for sanction by the Government of India. If there are schemes that provide for scholarships, but the funds are not provided or sanctioned in time, then budgetary allocations remain only in name and not in action.

Allocation for persons with disabilities – as per the 1995 legislation and not the rights of the persons with disabilities, Act 2016: There has been a marginal increment of Rs. 122.77 crores from the budget estimate of the Department for the empowerment of persons with disabilities for the financial year 2019-20. It is to be noted that almost all schemes that lead to the participation of persons with disabilities such as Assistance to Disabled Persons for purchasing/fitting of aids/appliances (ADIP), Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO), National Handicapped Finance and Development Corporation (NHFDC) show a declining trend. The Research and Rehabilitation Institutes and as well as the Institute of Sign Language find no allocation this financial year. Scheme for Implementation of Persons with Disabilities Act (SIPDA), which is looking at accessibility and district rehabilitation, finds a reduction of Rs.63.50 crore when compared to 2019-20 (BE). 

The budget allocates around Rs 251 crore towards the implementation of the 1995 Act, which only covered seven disabilities, and not 21 as mentioned under the new Act. A National Fund has been constituted to secure finances towards proper implementation of the Act of 2016, but the lack of budgetary allocations around it have rendered it meaningless. The Accessible India Campaign (AIC) which is one of the flagship programmes for accessibility does not find any mention in the Budget. Although the AIC was successful more on the level of creating a noise around accessibility, its vision was not translated on the ground due to lack of accountability framework and transparency. While hopes were pinned on its better implementation, lack of a financial framework has made it defunct.

*श्रीमती रमा देवी (शिवहर): मेरी समिति ने इस मंत्रालय के सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता विभाग तथा दिव्यांगजन सशक्तिकरण विभाग के प्रतिवेदन तैयार किए हैं और दोनों सदनों में 3 मार्च को प्रस्तुत किए हैं । 
  सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता विभाग से संबंधित प्रतिवेदन में समिति ने पाया कि 2019- 20 के दौरान विभाग को 8885 करोड़ रुपए का बजट आवंटित किया गया और विभाग ने 31 जनवरी, 2020 तक सिर्फ 5 हजार 740 करोड़ रुपए (5740.19) करोड़ रुपये का उपयोग किया जो आवंटित निधियों का 64.6 प्रतिशत था । समिति ने बाकी बची हुई उपयुक्त राशि को वापस किए जाने तथा आवंटित राशि का अनुसूचित जाति प्रभाग, पिछड़ा वर्ग प्रभाग तथा सोशल डिफेंस प्रभाग पर समय पर खर्च न करने पर खेद व्यक्त किया तथा यह आशा की कि विभाग वित्तीय वर्ष के अंत तक आवंटित राशि का पूर्व में उपयोग कर सकेगा । 
  मेरी समिति ने विभाग से संसदीय निर्वाचन क्षेत्र स्तरीय समितियों का गठन किए जाने तथा इस समिति में उस निर्वाचन क्षेत्र संसद सदस्य की भागीदारी सुनिश्चित करने की सिफारिश की है क्योंकि स्थानीय प्रतिनिधि अपने निर्वाचन क्षेत्र में आरक्षित जाति अन्य पिछड़ा वर्ग, वरिष्ठ नागरिकों और दिव्यांगजनों के कल्याण के लिए विभाग द्वारा क्रियान्वित की जा रही योजनाओं हेतु निधि की प्राप्ति की निगरानी कर सकते हैं और इन कार्यों की जमीनी हकीकत से अवगत होते हैं । 
  बाबू जगजीवन राम छात्रावास योजना जो अनुसूचित जाति के छात्रों के लिए छात्रावास के निर्माण का कार्य करती है तथा छात्रों को बेहतर शिक्षा देने की सिफारिश करती है, इसमें अब तक विभाग द्वारा किया गया प्रयास निराशाजनक है । इस कारण समिति ने विभाग से यह सिफारिश की है कि वह अपने कार्य में तेजी लाए जिससे यह योजना अपने उद्देश्य की प्राप्ति में सफल हो । साथ ही मद्यपान तथा नशीले पदार्थ दुरुपयोग निवारण हेतु योजना के बेहतर कार्यान्वयन के लिए समिति ने विभाग से यह सिफारिश की है कि वह मादक पदार्थ व्यवसनी व्यक्तियों, ट्रैफि‍क चौराहों आदि जगहों पर पहचान कर उनके कल्याण हेतु सुधारात्मक कदम उठाए । 
  इसी तरह दिव्यांगजन सशक्तिकरण विभाग की 2020- 21 की अनुदान की मांगों से यह ज्ञात होता है कि विभाग को 1204.90 करोड़ रुपए का बजट आवंटित किया गया था जिसे घटाकर 1100 करोड़ रुपए कर दिया गया और फरवरी 2020 तक वास्तविक व्‍यय केवल 669.90 करोड़ रुपया है । 
  इसलिए समिति ने पाया कि वित्तीय वर्ष की पहली तीन तिमाहियों में व्यय की गति काफी धीमी है और बजट का लगभग 40% हिस्से का उपयोग नहीं किया गया । इसलिए समिति ने विभाग से यह चाहा कि वह जिला अधिकारियों तथा राज्‍य के अधिकारियों के उपयोग के लिए अपनी प्रमुख योजनाओं का एक मसौदा प्रस्ताव तैयार करे जिसका उपयोग दिशानिर्देश रूपी दस्तावेज के रूप में ही हो सके । 
  दिव्यांगजन बहनों एवं भाइयों को उपकरण प्रदान करने वाली एडिप योजना के अंतर्गत एलिम्को एक सरकारी संस्‍थान है जिसके द्वारा विनिर्मित सहायक यंत्रों एवं उपकरणों की गुणवत्ता बनाए रखने के लिए स्वस्थ प्रतिस्पर्धा की आवश्यकता है । इसलिए समिति ने यह चाहा है कि विभाग एलिम्को के साथ प्रतिस्पर्धा करने के लिए इन उपकरणों के निर्माण में दक्षता वाली अन्य एजेंसियों की सूची बनाने पर विचार करे जिससे न केवल उत्पादन की गुणवत्ता में सुधार होगा साथ ही उनकी लागत में भी कमी आएगी  । 
 समिति ने यह पाया की देश में लगभग 42 लाख विद्यालय हैं और उनमें से अधिकतर दूरदराज एवं दुर्गम क्षेत्रों में स्थित हैं । चूंकि दिव्यांग छात्रों को भी सामान्य विद्यार्थियों में पढ़ने का पूर्ण अधिकार है । इसलिए समिति ने विभाग से यह आग्रह किया कि क्षेत्र के प्रत्येक स्कूल जियो टैग करें जिससे विभाग द्वारा शिक्षकों के लिए जो प्रशिक्षण का मॉड्यूल बनाया गया है उससे कोई भी स्कूल, अध्यापक वंचित न रहे और दिव्यांगता के कारण कोई भी बच्चा इन विद्यालयों में शिक्षा ग्रहण करने से वंचित ना रहे ।

* SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB (CUTTACK): At the outset let me first ask, why some are poor? The answer is, they are denied opportunities. Because of inequality in the distribution of income among people, poverty has arisen. Depravity of opportunity is the cause of poverty. Moreover, extreme or absolute poverty, experienced by those whose income is barely sufficient for survival, remains widespread in our country. Extreme poverty and the suffering, it entails affect a large proportion of humankind, and major efforts by Government and international organisations to reduce or eradicate poverty have thus failed to produce the desired results. 

Do these facts and trends suggest a regression in social justice? The answer to this question, if considered within the framework of the Charter of the United Nations and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights is not unequivocal. The persistence, aggravation and very existence of extreme poverty constitute an injustice. Those experiencing dire poverty are deprived of a number of the fundamental rights invoked in the charter and enumerated in the Universal Declaration. Hunger is but one face of poverty; discrimination poor health, vulnerability, insecurity and a lack of personal and professional development opportunities are among the many other challenges faced by the poor.

Unlike justice in the broad sense, social justice is a relatively recent concept born of the struggles surrounding the industrial revolution and advent of socialist views on the organisation of society. In our country, Government through its programmes and schemes is striving to build an inclusive society wherein Members of the target groups are provided adequate support for their growth and development.

When I am putting my views on the Demands for Grants on Social Justice and Empowerment 2020-2021. As this Ministry is responsible for the welfare and empowerment of certain disadvantaged sections of the society such as Scheduled Castes; Other Backward Classes, persons with disabilities, senior citizens, victims of substance abuse and transgender persons, it implements various schemes and programmes for the welfare of disadvantaged sections. I come to know that this year the funds allocated for the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment the upcoming financial year has a decline of around 11 percent, Rs.8885 crore from Rs.9963.25 crore which is the revised estimates in 2018-19. On a cursory look into the funds allocated, it is found that the extent of under-utilisation has been 18% in 2013-14. However, in 2016-17 the under utilization was down to 1%. In 2017-18 the Ministry revised estimates expect expenditure to be 1% more than the budgeted allocation. 

One of the reasons for under utilization is lack of expenditure of funds by the North East States. It is marked that there is failure on the part of North Eastern States to send their utilization certificates within time, leading to lapse of funds and low demand for funds from these states. In 2019-20 Rs.8885 crore was budgeted but Rs.5740.19 crore were utilised by 31st January, 2020 which was 64.6 percent of the total allotted funds. By 15th February, 2020, the utilisation increased to Rs.6644.85 crore which became 74.79 percent of the total allocated funds as RE was Rs.8885 crore, why there is this uneven pace of utilisation of funds? Why is it so slow in the first three quarters of the year. Almost 35 percent of the budget remained unutilised despite the revised instruction of the Ministry of Finance that Ministry and Departments could only utilise only 25 percent of their BE in the last quarter of the financial year. It is learnt that late submission of UCs and non-receipt of complete proposals are the main reasons for the delay in full utilisation of allocated budget, can't there be a guideline issued stating that release of every instalment of funds to States there should be a deadline for submitting UCs.

Take for example the case of utilisation of the resources by the Scheduled Caste Division since 2017-18 which shows that in the year 2017- 18 and 2018-19 Rs.34.18 crore and Rs.21.67 crore were surrendered due to non-utilisation of the funds. Similarly, in the year 2019-20 out of Rs.6135 crore, this Division could utilised Rs.3980 crore only, till the end of January 2020, leaving the rest Rs. 2155 crore to be spent in the remaining two months of the financial year. That means 35 percent of the allocated resources remained unspent till the end of January 2020. The spending pattern of the Backward Classes Division shows that it has surrendered Rs.65.69 crore in 2017-18 overspent Rs.22 crore in 2018-19 and spent Rs.1174 crore out of Rs.1833 crore in the year 2019-20 till the end of January 2020, leaving the rest Rs.659 crore to be spent in the remaining two months.

I would like to draw the attention of the Minister relating to Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC Students which is one of the oldest and most important scheme with the objective to provide financial assistance to SC students to enable them to pursue post matric education. It is always found that funds are not released due to lack of complete proposals by the State authorities in time.

A suggestion has been mooted by the Standing Committee on Social Justice and Empowerment that similar to the Committee created by Ministry of Road, Transport and Highways for every Parliamentary Constituency be created so that local represetatives become well aware of the ground realities of their constituencies. They can monitor the progress of the schemes and programmes and become aware about the welfare of SCs, OBCs, Senior citizens and other targeted groups.

It is learnt that a proposal for transferring funds directly into the Bank accounts of SC students under Direct Benefit Transfer is still awaiting approval of the Cabinet. It needs to be pursued vigorously. It is also learnt that a proposal is there before the Committee to increase the share of the Centre from 90:10 to 60:40. This only look as an extra burden on them. Construction of hostels for Scheduled Castes students is not working. The Department is unable to spend the allocated money which depicts a dismal picture. Except Kerala, which has established 100 hostels and the rest are just sprinkling, it's very disappointing. Can we know the reasons why other States could not do it?

One is also alarmed that after a lapse of three years since 2016, Transgender Persons are yet to receive any support from the Government. Hardly any money been allocated. There is a need for higher allocations for the welfare of Transgender community. There is a need to provide a separate scheme for OBCs so that they can improve their skill and can be gainfully employed.

I am aware that National Action Plan for Skill Training for PWDs under SIPDA was launched by the Department in collaboration with Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship(MSDE) in 2015 with the objective of training PWDs to enable them to have gainful employment. However to my utter dismay, even after reducing the beneficiary target from 50,000 to 20,000 beneficiaries in February, 2020 for the year 2019-20, the Department could only provide skills to a miniscule 457 beneficiaries in the first three and half quarters of the fiscal. You may be confident of achieving the target in terms of number of trained beneficiaries in the light of MIS Portal being developed by it, but it is a herculean task that in the remaining part of the financial year and even have set an revised target this year appears to be difficult. Nonetheless, I would urge the Government to strive for it and also strengthen the employability of the beneficiaries after they complete the skill training. It would be better to maintain the data of beneficiaries who got employed after getting skill training under the programme and use this data as input for future streamlining of the scheme, if need be. 

I would like to draw the attention of the Minister towards District Disability Rehabilitation Centres (DDRCs) which were started as outreach activity of the Ministry for providing comprehensive services to the PWDs at grassroot level and for facilitating creation of the infrastructure and capacity building at the district level for awareness generation, rehabilitation and training of rehabilitation professionals. 

It has come to light that as of now 325 districts have been identified for setting up of District Disability Rehabilitation Centres(DDRCs) and out of 325 identified Districts, DDRCs have been set up in 264 districts. The funds have been released only to 92 Districts for the last four years and current year. Can the Government tell us the specific reasons for non-functioning of large number of DDRCs set up and the specific measures taken to address them?

DDRCs of Tripura and Sikkim even do not have complete address available in the Ministry's Annual Report? This scheme needs to be revisited and be recast so that it can become workable.

It is gratifying to note that Government has generated and issued 32.50 lakh Unique Disability Identity (UDID) Cards in 682 districts and have started a drive further to speed up the generation of UDID Cards. It is also found that 1.5 crore Legacy Certificates have been taken on board in the Unique Identification Cards System, an online Portal. Now States are required to just upload the revalidated Certificate to generate a UDID Card and medical examination will be required only for newer disabilities listed in new RPWD Act, 2016. Even for that, the procedure has been streamlined and norms for constitution of medical teams have been relaxed. However, performance of some States is still quite poor, for instance in Manipur only 737 cards were issued as against grant of Rs.28 lakh and in West Bengal a total of 4 cards were issued against Rs. 3 lakh funds. Many States and UTs, like Bihar, Assam, Telangana, Tripura, Andhra Pradesh etc. did not receive any funds till 2018-19. In this connection, I would appreciate the Department initiation of a colour coded daily performance report with indicated level of performance of lagging States/UTs and following it up with States/UTs/ Districts on daily basis to monitor the progress made by them. I hope that Department will continue with their efforts to bring all the States and UTs on board and complete the project at the earliest.

There has always been a demand to have a caste census in the country. Last caste census was done in 1931 which is around 90 years ago. This is required because as provisions are being made for upliftment of disadvantageous section of the society the administration should get the data, factually correct data of the targeted group. I urge upon the Government to take steps to include more column in the question when Census in numeration is done of every citizen.

Reservation is nothing else but positive intervention to help the society to grow. No nation can grow, when a large section of the Society languish in poverty because of deprivation. The country has come a long way indeed during last some decades. It should be continued.

SHRI RAGHU RAMA KRISHNA RAJU (NARSAPURAM): Hon. Chairperson, I am thankful to you for giving me this opportunity to speak on this very important subject, that is, Demands for Grants under the control of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for the year 2020-21.

In this regard, I really appreciate the efforts of our hon. Minister, Shri Thawar Chand Gehlot-ji for getting an increase of 14 per cent in this trivial situation, where financial crisis is there. Despite that, with his zeal and commitment, he has been able to get 14 per cent increase in allocation. I really appreciate him. We have the leadership of our beloved hon. Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi-ji, who has come from the lower level to the highest level in the country, and who has been the role model not only for the country but also for the world. His initiatives are very well reflected through the hon. Minister in these Demands for Grants. 

While I say so, I would like to bring in a few suggestion that are needed. We have the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana for the elderly people in our country. We have close to 10.5 crore elderly people wherein 70 per cent of them have been residing in rural India. This is a good scheme to supply them kits, handsticks, and little automation devices for their wellbeing at that age. Our culture says that we all must respect our elders. The way how we respect our elders is to take care of them in the best manner. But unfortunately, the budget allocated for such a good scheme has been drastically reduced to Rs. 1 crore.

I would sincerely urge our hon. Minister with good heart that let us remember them, and increase this budget allocation to the required levels. It is the need of the hour. 

I really appreciate that they have increased the budget allocation for prevention of manual scavengers by 400 per cent. For every scheme including Pre-Matric Scholarships and Post-Matric Scholarships, there has been a very good increase in the budget allocation. 

Sir, here, I would be failing in my duty if I do not mention about my beloved leader, Shri Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, who has brought in several reforms with regard to the upliftment of BCs. Just to cite an example, in the recent Rajya Sabha elections, out of four seats, two seats were given to BCs. We have given up to 59 per cent reservations for BCs and SCs. That way, as a great social reformer – though he is the youngest Chief Minister in the country – he has come up with various reforms where in all the temples and elsewhere, he has given 50 per cent reservations for OBCs and SCs.

That way, in the modern age, while we talk of great reformers like Jyotirao Phule-ji and Ambedkar-ji in the past, now I would not hesitate -- though he is a very young man – to praise my leader for bringing in these kinds of schemes for the upliftment of EBCs in a genuine manner. 

For such a young Chief Minister, I would also seek the support of the Central Government by going through various such schemes.

There is one important point though it may not be directly relevant to the Demands for Grants. But earlier also, I had made a representation to the hon. Minister, and I would like to reiterate it here. It is with regard to the same subject. There is a community by name Turpu Kapu, Gajula Kapu in our State, who predominantly reside in the northern part of coastal Andhra in the Vizag, Srikakulam and Vizianagaram Districts. But for their livelihood, some of these people have started migrating to other Districts. The same community, which is in the serial number 19 in the List are considered as OBCs only in the three Districts. But whoever has gone to other Districts for their livelihood, are being considered as forward caste people. The father is there as OBC, but his sons or grandsons, who are staying in Vijayawada or some other District for livelihood, are being treated as forward caste.

It is very unfair, Sir. We have brought this to the notice of the hon. Minister earlier. He has responded very positively. Some commission has to be formed in this regard. Though this is not the right forum yet I request the hon. Minister to kindly consider this issue which is a major issue and as a State, we cannot do this. The State has also made several representations. I urge the Minister to kindly consider this. 

We are all with you as far as the Demands for Grants are concerned. Thank you so much. 

श्री दुलाल चंद्र गोस्वामी (कटिहार): धन्यवाद, सभापति महोदय ।

इस मांग के समर्थन में मुझे बोलने का मौका दिया, इसके लिए आपका धन्यवाद । वर्ष 2020-21 के लिए सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय के नियंत्रणाधीन अनुदानों की मांगों पर चर्चा में भाग लेते हुए मैं यह कहना चाहता हूं कि यह मंत्रालय एक अत्यंत ही महत्वपूर्ण मंत्रालय है । मंत्रालय द्वारा हमारे आसपास की सभी समस्याओं के प्रति बहुत ही सजगता से और सामाजिक, शैक्षणिक, आर्थिक रूप से उपेक्षित वर्ग के सशक्तीकरण एवं उनकी समस्याओं के प्रति महत्वपूर्ण जिम्मेदारी निभाता है ।

इस दिशा में हमारे माननीय मंत्री थावर चंद गहलोत जी ने बखूबी पिछली सरकार में भी इसका कार्यभार सुचारू रूप से सफलतापूर्वक संचालित करते आ रहे हैं । उनकी कार्य कुशलता के लिए हम उनको बधाई देते हैं । उन्होंने समाज के सभी वर्गों का ध्यान रखते हुए जिस प्रकार से काम किया है, अभी हाल ही में सरकार द्वारा 300 दिव्यांग ट्राईसाइकिलों से लगभग दो किलोमीटर परेड और दूसरा, 400 व्हीलचेयर द्वारा परेड और तीसरा, 626 ट्राईसाइकिलों का एक घंटे में माननीय प्रधान मंत्री जी द्वारा इसका वितरण किया गया और यह एक विश्व कीर्तिमान स्थापित हुआ । इस काम के लिए भी मैं विभाग और केन्द्र सरकार की प्रशंसा करता हूं । यह समरसता और न्याय का प्रतीक है । मैं इसके लिए पुन: सरकार को धन्यवाद देता हूं ।

महोदय, अनूसूचित जातियां एवं अन्य पिछड़ा वर्ग, वरिष्ठ नागरिक, मद्यपान एवं नशीले पदार्थ के दुरुपयोग से पीड़ित थर्ड जेंडर व्यक्ति, भिखारी, विमुक्त तथा घुमन्तू जातियां – डी एंड टी और आर्थिक रूप से पिछड़ा वर्ग – ईवीसी तथा आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्ग – ईडब्ल्यूएस इसमें शामिल हैं । इन्हें सरकार से काफी अपेक्षा है, खासकर उन राज्यों में, जो आज भी विकास की दौड़ में पिछड़े हुए हैं । वहां के विकास कार्य को गति देने के साथ-साथ कमजोर वर्गों को विशेष सहायता देने की योजना केन्द्र सरकार द्वारा चलाया जाना जरूरी है, जैसा कि बिहार में है । हमारे बिहार के आदरणीय मुख्य मंत्री जी ने सभी वरिष्ठ नागरिकों को वृद्धजन पेंशन योजना से आच्छादित किया  है । 

माननीय मंत्री जी, इसकी एक बहुत बड़ी खूबी है कि अगर पति और पत्नी की 60 वर्ष की उम्र है तो भी पति और पत्नी, दोनों को ही इसके कवर के दायरे में लिया गया है । मैं चाहूंगा कि इस महत्वपूर्ण योजना को केन्द्र सरकार पूरे देश में लागू करे । खासकर, जो वरिष्ठ नागरिक हैं, वरिष्ठ असहाय व्यक्ति हैं, विधवा, दिव्यांग, विमुक्त तथा घुमन्तु जाति के लोग, थर्ड-जेंडर को भी इस योजना में शामिल करना चाहिए, ताकि उन्हें अपना जीवन-यापन करने में सहूलियत हो । मैं यहां एक बात और माननीय मंत्री जी से कहना चाहूंगा कि वृद्धा पेंशन की राशि 500 रुपये देते हैं । यहां हम केन्द्र सरकार से मांग करते हैं कि पेंशन की राशि कम से कम एक हजार रुपये होनी चाहिए । पिछले 6 वर्षों से लगातार मंत्रालय के बजट में बढ़ोतरी यह दर्शाती है कि सरकार कमजोर वर्गों के उत्थान के लिए सजग है । वर्तमान वर्ष के लिए 1 लाख करोड़ रुपये से अधिक राशि का आबंटन काफी सराहनीय है । 

महोदय, समाज में विशेषकर अनुसूचित जाति के उत्थान और उनके कल्याण के लिए आर्थिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्ग के सभी वर्गों के लिए 223 स्कीमों के तहत केन्द्र सरकार योजनाओं को संचालित कर रही है । इससे समाज में जो खाई बनी हुई थी, उसे पाटने के लिए केन्द्र सरकार महत्वपूर्ण काम कर रही है । इस प्रकार ओ.बी.सी. वर्ग के लिए भी विशेष ध्यान देने की आवश्यकता है । वे भी समाज के विकास की मुख्य धारा में अभी पिछड़े हुए हैं । उनको बराबरी का स्थान दिलाने के लिए विशेष योजना चलाने की आवश्यकता है । 

सरकार ने छात्रवृत्ति की पात्रता के लिए भी काफी लचीला रुख अपनाया है और आय की सीमा में छूट दी है । यह काफी सराहनीय कदम है । मैं यहां कहना चाहूंगा कि बिहार सरकार के द्वारा बिहार में मुख्य मंत्री ग्रामीण परिवहन योजना के तहत एस.सी./एस.टी. और ओ.बी.सी. को व्यावसायिक वाहन हेतु कोई छोटा व्यावसायिक वाहन खरीदने के लिए 1 लाख रुपये तक की अनुदान राशि या फिर 50 % तक का अनुदान देती है । 

दूसरी बात यह है कि मुख्य मंत्री एस.सी./एस.टी. और ओ.बी.सी. उद्यमिता योजना के तहत बिहार सरकार 10 लाख रुपये लोन देती है, जिसमें 5 लाख रुपये अनुदान है और 5 लाख रुपये की राशि उनको बिना सूद लौटानी है । निश्चित रूप से यह इस समाज के उत्थान के लिए महत्वपूर्ण कदम है । मैं भारत सरकार से मांग करूंगा कि इसके प्रति भारत सरकार एक सकारात्मक रुख अपनाये और बिहार सरकार की इस योजना को अपनाए ।

मैं दो और महत्वपूर्ण विषयों पर सदन का ध्यान आकृष्ट करना चाहता हूं । समाज में जो विक्षिप्तजन हैं, जो समाज में यत्र-तत्र अपने परिवार, अपने सगे-संबंधियों से अलग होकर घूम रहे हैं, मैं भारत सरकार से मांग करता हूं कि ऐसे विक्षिप्त जनों के लिए विशेष शेल्टर होम बनाए । सामूहिक रूप से रखकर उनका इलाज हो । यह जिला लेवल पर इन विक्षिप्तजन के लिए हो । यह निश्चित रूप से एक सभ्य समाज और हम लोगों के लिए बड़ी चिंता का विषय है । उसी तरह से जो भिक्षु हैं, समाज में हम लोग देखते हैं कि वे जहां-तहां सामूहिक जगहों पर रहते हैं । वे भिक्षाटन कर रहे हैं, चाहे आप रेलवे स्टेशनों पर चले जाइए या कहीं भी चले जाइए, लेकिन बिहार सरकार ने, बिहार के मुख्य मंत्री आदरणीय नीतीश कुमार जी ने इस पर बहुत अच्छा काम किया है । उन्होंने भिक्षावृत्ति निवारण नीति बिहार में बनाई है और इस दिशा में बड़ा काम कर रहे हैं । 

मैं अंत में एक महत्वपूर्ण बात रखना चाहूंगा, जो पूरे देश और सदन के लिए भी महत्वपूर्ण  है । मैं उसके लिए थोड़ा समय चाहूंगा । वर्ष 2020-21 में जनगणना होनी है, आर्थिक सामाजिक जनगणना होनी है । इस जनगणना का बड़ा ही महत्व है । जो जनगणना होगी, उसमें मैं सरकार से मांग करता हूं कि जातिगत आधार पर जनगणना का प्रावधान होना चाहिए । इससे समाज के सभी वर्गों की जातियों के बारे सही आंकड़े प्राप्त होंगे और भविष्य में इन आंकड़ों के माध्यम से समाज के जो कमजोर वर्ग हैं, उनकी योजनाओं के विकास में सहायक सिद्ध होंगे । वर्ष 1931 के बाद, आजादी के बाद दोबारा जातिगत जनगणना नहीं हुई है । मैं इसके लिए माननीय मंत्री जी और भारत सरकार से निवेदन करूंगा कि जाति आधारित जनगणना हो । 

एक छोटी सी बात और कहना चाहता हूं । मैं जिस राज्य से आता हूं, वह बिहार राज्य है और बिहार राज्य में दो-तीन तरह की जातियां हैं । एक किसान जाति है और किसान जाति का पर्यायवाची कृषि वैश्य चसौट है । चसौट का मतलब किसानी करने वाला होता है । किसान जाति को आरक्षण का लाभ मिल रहा है, लकिन कृषि वैश्य चसौट को लाभ नहीं मिल रहा है । उसी तरह से एक राजवंशी जाति है, जिसे पश्चिम बंगाल में अनुसूचित जनजाति का लाभ ‍मिलता है, लेकिन बिहार राज्य में नहीं मिलता है । अत: इन जातियों के साथ अन्याय न हो, इनको भी अनुसूचित जनजाति का लाभ मिले, तो इनका भी विकास अन्य अनुसूचित जनजाति के लोगों की भांति हो सकेगा । आपने मुझे समय दिया, इसके लिए धन्यवाद । 

* SHRIMATI SUMALATHA AMBAREESH (MANDYA) : I would like to highlight some of the significant issues to draw the attention of the Government. 

As far as welfare of Senior citizens and elderly persons is concerned the Government is taking various steps, But there is a need to ensure the effective implementation of the schemes for elderly persons. As we are all aware that there has been a steady rise in the population of older persons in India. The number of elder persons has increased from 1.98 crore in 1951 to 7.6 crore in 2001, and 10.38 crore in 2011. The projections indicate that the number of people in the age group of 60+ in India will increase to 14.3 crore in 2021 and 17.3 crore in 2026.

The traditional norms and values of the Indian society taught us on showing respect and providing care for the aged. However, in recent times, society is witnessing a change in the joint family system, as a result of which a large number of parents are being neglected by their families exposing them to lack of emotional, physical and financial support. These older persons are facing a lot of problems in the absence of adequate social security. This clearly reveals that ageing has become a major social challenge and there is a need to provide for the economic and health needs of the elderly and to create a social milieu, which is conducive and sensitive to the emotional needs of the elderly. 

Hence, I would like to urge upon the Government to take all necessary measures to ensure that the Senior Citizens are provided the basic amenities like shelter, food, medical care and entertainment opportunities to lead happy and comfortable life in the fag-end of their life. 

As per the Census 2011, in India, out of the 121 crore population, about 2.68 crore persons are ‘disabled’ which is 2.21% of the total population. In an era where ‘inclusive development’ is being emphasized as the right path towards sustainable development, focused initiatives for the welfare of disabled persons are essential. This emphasizes the need for strengthen the existing mechanism to deal the issues pertaining to persons with disabilities in the country. People with disabilities are vulnerable because of the many barriers we face : attitudinal, physical, and financial. Addressing these barriers is within our reach and we have a moral duty to do so. There is a need to unlock the potential of so many disabled people to provide them an opportunity to contribute to the world. So, I would like to impress upon the Government to make sure that the persons with disabilities are provided access to health, rehabilitation, support, education, and employment-and they get the chance to shine. 

The Government has introduced various scholarship schemes to Promote education by covering the basic costs of Studying, tuition fees or providing financial help to students. There are several Scholarships for Students from schooling and college studies. Namely pre-matric, post-matric some scholarships are for undergraduate, postgraduate courses and PhD level. However there is a need to have a rationalization in giving scholarships to students. Government should ensure that every deserved student are recognized for his or her talent and fulfil their educational needs. It should be made available to all category of students including girls, minority students, college students etc., Apart from this adequate provisions for funding for the scholarship should be made by the Government.

The Government has implemented Free Coaching scheme to enable students to clear the competitive exams and secure job opportunities. The scheme is targeted towards providing coaching of quality education for economically disadvantaged Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) to enable them to appear in competitive examination and succeed in obtaining an appropriate job. However, there is a need for enhancing the funds for the scheme to make sure that the scheme is available to all eligible candidates in the country. Even after 7 decades of independence and in spite of various measures taken to improve the level of education in the country, literacy levels among Backward classes, particularly among women, continues to be low. 

The Government has taken several measures to improve the literacy rate among women and as a result considerable progress has been achieved in improving the level of literacy and education in the country. However, there is still a long way to go before respectable levels of literacy are achieved. It has been recognized that educational and economic support for Backward Classes has not been adequate and there is disparity between Backward Classes and the non- backward sections of the population at every level.

The position of women in terms of literacy among OBC’s population is also a cause of concern. Considering the important role of women in shaping the size of the family and outlook of its members, investment in improving education among women of these communities will not only improve their social and economic status, but will also help in accelerating the socio-economic development of these communities and the nation as a whole. It is self-evident and universally accepted fact that education is one of the key instruments of effective development of weaker sections. The education facilities are not evenly distributed throughout the country. Many a times students from rural areas especially those belonging to weaker sections have to give up their educational pursuits for the reason that adequate hostel facilities are not available for them in the quality education centers. Hence, I would like to request the Union Government to enhance the allocation of funds for construction of Hostels for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) Boys and Girls.

In my Parliamentary Constituency Mandya district in Karnataka more than 50% hostels don’t have own buildings. They are running in the rented accommodation. In Mandya district there are 49 Pre-Matric Boys hostels and 16 Pre-Matric Girls hostels are functioning. Out of them 32 boys hostels and 7 girls hostels have own buildings. Remaining 25 hostels for both Pre-Matric boys and girls are running in rented buildings. The construction work of 1 boys and 3 girls hostels are in progress. However there is a need to take steps for construction of 13 boys and 8 girls hostels. As far as Post-Matric boys and girls hostels are concerned 23 boys and 21 girls hostels are there, among them only 9 boys hostels and 4 girls hostels are functioning in own buildings. Remaining 14 boys and 17 girls’ post- matric hostels are running in the rented buildings. Of them construction of 2 boys and 4 girls post-Matric hostel are under progress. However, 25 hostels buildings for both boys and girls are yet to start the construction. Therefore, I would like to request the Union Government to kindly take necessary steps to start the construction of hostels with allocation of funds as all these hostels have got allotted the required land for construction of hostels. I hope the Government will take immediate positive measures in this regard.

श्री गिरीश चन्द्र (नगीना): सभापति महोदय, आपने मुझे सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय के लिए मांगी गई वित्तीय वर्ष-2020-21 के बजट पर अपने विचार व्यक्त करने के लिए मौका दिया, इसके लिए मैं आपका आभार प्रकट करता हूं । आपके माध्यम से मैं सरकार का ध्यान विगत् वर्षों से मांगी गयी धनराशि तथा सरकार द्वारा मंजूर की गई धनराशि की तरफ आकर्षित कराना चाहता हूं । वर्ष 2016-17 में 106.47 करोड़ रुपया सरकार से मांगा गया था, लेकिन सरकार द्वारा 65.66 करोड़ रुपये ही मंजूर किए गए । इसी प्रकार वर्ष 2017-18 में मांगी गई धनराशि 103.56 करोड़ रुपए थी, लेकिन उसके सापेक्ष मंजूर की गई धनराशि 69.08 करोड़ रुपये सरकार ने स्वीकृत की । वर्ष 2018-19 में वर्ष 2017-18 में मांगी गई धनराशि से 12 प्रतिशत अधिक मांग की गई थी और सरकार द्वारा 77.50 करोड़ रुपये मंजूर किए गए थे । इन आंकड़ों को बताने का मेरा आशय सिर्फ इतना है कि एक तरफ जहां दिन-प्रतिदिन जनसंख्या अपना विस्फोटक रूप धारण करती जा रही है और दूसरी तरफ जनता के हितों के लिए दी जाने वाली सामाजिक सरोकारिता से संबंधित धनराशि ऐसी लगती है, मानो ऊंट के मुंह में जीरा । इसी कड़ी में पोस्ट मैट्रिक छात्रवृत्ति के लिए विभाग या मंत्रालय उसको मिलने वाले कुल बजट का 38.7 प्रतिशत धन खर्च करता है ।

महोदय, वर्ष 2018-19 में जो बजट मंत्रालय को दिया गया था, वर्ष 2017-18 के रिवाइज्ड एस्टिमेट में 10.4 प्रतिशत कम करके दिया गया । मुझे आशंका है कि इस बार भी सरकार एस्टिमेट रिवाइज करके ही दिए जाने वाले धन की अनुशंसा करेगी । आपके माध्यम से मैं सरकार से अनुरोध करना चाहता हूं कि इस बार रिवाइज्ड एस्टिमेट से धन को कम न किया जाए । रिहैबिलिटेशन ऑफ मैनुअल एस्क्वेंजर योजना के तहत जितना बजट दिया गया है, गत वर्षों में वह धन शत-प्रतिशत इस्तेमाल किया गया है । इसके लिए मैं सरकार को धन्यवाद करना चाहता हूं । इन मदों में दिए जाने वाले धन की कटौती सरकार न करे, सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय समाज से वंजित तबके के लोगों को विकसित कर राष्ट्र की मुख्य धारा से जोड़ने के लिए बना है । 

महोदय, मैं आपके माध्यम से सरकार से अनुरोध करना चाहूंगा कि सामाजिक न्याय व अधिकारिता मंत्रालय के अंतर्गत काम करने वाले डॉक्टर भीम राव अम्बेडकर फाउंडेशन को भी अधिक से अधिक धन मुहैया कराया जाए, जिससे दबे-कुचले, दलित व पिछड़े समाज के लोगों का चतुर्मुखी विकास हो सके । इसी कड़ी में मैं बताना चाहूंगा कि पिछले वर्षों में संस्थान द्वारा डॉक्टर भीमराव अम्बेडकर लाइब्रेरी नामक एक योजना संचालित की गई है, जिससे मुख्य रूप से आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर, गरीब, दलित तथा पिछड़े समाज के बच्चे लाभान्वित होते रहे हैं । सरकार ने यह योजना अब बन्द कर रखी है । मेरा यह कहना है कि यदि लोगों के चतुर्मुखी विकास के लिए सरकार कटिबद्ध है तो लाइब्रेरी की योजना अविलम्ब चालू करे और इसके लिए समुचित धन अलग से मुहैया कराने का काम सरकार करे । 

महोदय, मैं सरकार से यह जरूर कहना चाहूंगा कि जब उत्तर प्रदेश में बहुजन समाज पार्टी की सरकार थी, तो अनुसूचित जाति, जनजाति के बच्चों को जीरो बैलेंस पर एडमिशन दिलाकर उन बच्चों को बीटेक, एमटेक, एलएलबी और एमबीबीएस कराने का काम हमारी सरकार ने किया था । 

लेकिन आज जो अनुसूचित जाति और अनुसूचित जनजाति के छात्र हैं, जो शिक्षा ग्रहण कर रहे हैं, उनको सरकार से छात्रवृत्ति नहीं मिली है, जिसके कारण वह समाज, जो दबा-कुचला समाज है, अनुसूचित जाति और अनुसूचति जनजाति के बच्चे शिक्षा ग्रहण करने में कमी महसूस कर रहे  हैं । मैं चाहूंगा कि जिन छात्रों ने अपनी शिक्षा पूर्ण कर ली है, उसके बाद भी उनको छात्रवृत्ति उत्तर प्रदेश के स्कूलों में नहीं पहुंची है, जिसके कारण इन बच्चों का भविष्य अंधकारमय है । उन बच्चों की तरफ ध्यान रखते हुए मैं आपसे कहना चाहूंगा कि उत्तर प्रदेश के जितने भी छात्र-छात्राएं हैं, उनके लिए आप अविलम्ब सरकार से यह कहें कि शीघ्र उनको छात्रवृत्ति देकर शिक्षा में योगदान देने का काम आपकी सरकार करे । धन्यवाद ।

*श्री अनिल फिरोजिया (उज्जैन): अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के लोगों पर होने वाले अत्याचार और उनके साथ होने वाले भेदभाव को रोकने के मकसद से अनुसूचित जाति और अनुसूचित जनजाति (अत्‍याचार निवारण) अधिनियम, 1989 बनाया गया था । इसके तहत इन लोगों को समाज में एक समान दर्जा दिलाने के लिए कई प्रावधान किए गए और इनकी हर संभव मदद के लिए जरूरी उपाय किए गए । 
  इन पर होने वाले अपराधों की सुनवाई के लिए विशेष व्यवस्था की गई ताकि ये अपनी बात खुल कर रख सके । हाल ही में एससीएसटी एक्ट को लेकर उबाल उस वक्त सामने आया, जब सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने इस कानून के प्रावधान में बदलाव किया और जब यह बदलाव के कारण कमजोर महसूस किया जा रहा था । लेकिन अनुसूचित जाति व अनुसूचित जनजाति के भाई बहनों पर होने वाले अत्याचारों को रोकने के लिए व उन्हें न्याय दिलाने के लिए कटिबद्ध हमारी सरकार और माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी एवं माननीय सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्री जी ने बिना देर किए सदन में संशोधन बिल लेकर आए और अनुसूचित जाति जनजाति के भाई-बहनों को न्याय दिलाने के लिए सशक्त प्रावधान किए । इस कारण देश भर के कुछ हिस्सों में इस बिल को समझे बिना कुछ लोगों ने परदे के पीछे रहकर विरोध भी करवाया लेकिन माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी की दृढ़ इच्छा शक्ति के चलते नया संशोधन आज भी अडिग है  । 
 इतना ही नहीं यह सरकार हर वर्ग की सरकार है इस बात को चरितार्थ करते हुए माननीय प्रधानमंत्री एवं माननीय मंत्री थावरचंद गहलोत जी ने लाखों गरीब सवर्ण परिवारों के अधिकारों का संरक्षण करने के लिए 10% आरक्षण की व्यवस्था की । सबसे बड़ी बात इसके लिए देश के संविधान में संशोधन करने की जरूरत थी, सरकार की दृढ़ इच्छाशक्ति द्वारा संशोधन किया गया व सबका साथ सबका विकास की परिणिति को चरितार्थ किया । मेरी नजर में यह सरकार का क्रांतिकारी कदम है । अनुसूचित जाति के अधिकारों के लिए जो संशोधन किए गए हैं वह एक सराहनीय पहल है । 
  मैं बड़े गर्व से बताना चाहता हूं कि यह ऐसी सरकार है जो चाहती है कि अनुसूचित जाति के होनहार छात्रों की पढ़ाई में रुपये बाधा न बने । इसके लिए इस सरकार ने श्री सुरेंद्र पाल पिता श्री जसपाल जी को 1 करोड़ 17 लाख 56 हजार, 352 रुपये की स्कॉलरशिप देकर उस गरीब विद्यार्थी का भविष्य तराशने का कार्य किया है । 
  ऐसे सैकड़ों से ज्यादा उदाहरण मेरे पास हैं जिसमें माननीय मंत्री जी ने विभाग के अंतर्गत आने वाले गरीब युवाओं को उनकी शिक्षा के लिए लाखों रुपए देकर उन्हें उच्च शिक्षा में अग्रणी स्थान पर खड़ा करने का कार्य किया है । सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय हेतु इस वित्त वर्ष के लिए 10,104 करोड़ रुपये का बजट पास किया गया है । 

इस वित्त वर्ष में हमारी सरकार ने वार्षिक कार्य योजना हेतु 2020- 21 के लिए बजट प्रावधान 2987. 33 करोड़ रुपए है । यह योजना बायब्रेट इंडिया के लिए प्रधानमंत्री यंग अचीवर्स स्कॉलरशिप अवार्ड योजना (पीएम यशस्वी) नामक योजना के अंतर्गत मंत्रालय की अन्य छात्रवृति योजनाओं के साथ मिलना प्रस्तावित किया गया है । 
  एससी और ओबीसी छात्रों के लिए निशुल्क कोचिंग प्रदान करने का प्रावधान किया गया है जिससे वो अपने निजी क्षेत्र में उपयुक्‍त रोजगार प्राप्त करने में सफल हो सकें । एससी छात्रों के लिए उत्कृष्ट श्रेणी की शिक्षा हेतु केंद्रीय क्षेत्र की संभावित छात्रवृत्ति स्कीम का भी प्रावधान किया गया है । इसी के साथ मैं और मेरे क्षेत्र की जनता की कुछ मांगे हैं जैसे कि हमारा मध्य प्रदेश, छत्तीसगढ़ अनुसूचित जाति, अनुसूचित जनजाति बाहुल्य क्षेत्र है, वहां के लोगों के लिए यूपीएससी, पीएससी, आर्मी, नवोदय और एनडीए की तैयारी के लिए अच्छी कोचिंग की सुविधा की व्यवस्था की जाए । 
  इन क्षेत्रों में छात्रावास की संख्या पर्याप्त नहीं है जिसके कारण विद्यार्थियों को काफी कठिनाइयों का सामना करना पड़ता है इसलिए मेरा माननीय मंत्री जी से अनुरोध है कि कृपया छात्रावास की संख्या बढ़ाई जाए ।

*श्री अशोक महादेवराव नेते (गडचिरोली चिमुर): माननीय प्रधानमंत्री आदरणीय मोदी जी एवं माननीय वित्त मंत्री आदरणीया निर्मला सीतारमण जी, का मैं हृदय से धन्यवाद करना चाहूंगा, क्योंकि यह बजट लीक से हटकर दिखाई दिया है, जिसमें लोक-लुभावन घोषणाओं के स्थान पर बजट को कृषि एवं किसानों, गरीब एवं मध्यमवर्गीय लोगों पर केंद्रित किया गया है । 
  माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व में सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय ने विगत वर्षों के दौरान शैक्षिक, आर्थिक और सामाजिक विकास संबंधी अपने विभिन्न कार्यक्रमों के माध्यम से समाज के उपेक्षित और अलग-अलग वर्गो- अनुसूचित जाति एवं अनुसूचित जनजातियों, अन्य पिछड़े वर्गों, वृद्धजनों और मद्यपान तथा नशीली दवा दुरुपयोग पीड़ितों को सशक्त बनाया है, ताकि वे सक्रिय सुरक्षित और सम्मानित जीवन जी सकें और अपनी सभी बुनियादी जरूरतों की पूर्ति कर सकें । वस्तुतः सरकार ने इन सभी के विकास के लिए समान अवसर सुनिश्चित किए जाने हेतु अथक प्रयास किए हैं, जो स्वागत योग्य हैं । 
  हमारे संविधान के अनुच्छेद 38 में उल्लिखित है कि राज्य ऐसी सामाजिक व्यवस्था करेगा जिसमें सामाजिक, आर्थिक और राजनैतिक न्याय राष्ट्रीय जीवन की सभी संस्थाओं को अनुप्रमाणित करे, भरसक रूप में स्थापना और संरक्षण करके लोक कल्याण की अभिवृद्धि का प्रयास करेगा तथा आय की असमानताओं को कम करने का प्रयास करेगा और साथ ही व्यक्तियों के बीच बल्कि विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में रहने वाले और विभिन्न व्यवसायों में लगे हुए लोगों के समूहों के बीच भी प्रतिष्ठा, सुविधाओं और अवसरों की असमानता समाप्त करने का प्रयास करेगा । 

संविधान के अनुच्छेद 41 और 46 में यह भी अंत: स्थापित है कि राज्‍य अपनी आर्थिक सामर्थ्य और विकास की सीमाओं के भीतर, काम पाने के, शिक्षा पाने के और बेकारी, बुढ़ापा, बीमारी और निशक्तता तथा अन्य अनर्जित अभाव की दशाओं में लोक सहायता पाने के अधिकार को प्राप्त कराने का प्रभावी उपबंध करेगा एवं जनता के दुर्बल वर्गों के, विशेषत: अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के शिक्षा और अर्थ संबंधी हितों की विशेष सावधानी से अभिवृद्धि करेगा एवं सामाजिक अन्याय तथा सभी प्रकार के शोषण से उनकी संरक्षा करेगा । 
  मुझे प्रसन्नता है कि आदरणीय श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व में सरकार ने इन सब दिशाओं में अभूतपूर्व कार्य किया है, जो स्वागत योग्य है । वास्‍तव में सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता विभाग का विजन एक ऐसे समाज का निर्माण करना है, जिसमें लक्ष्य समूह अपनी समृद्धि और विकास के पर्याप्त समर्थन के साथ उपयोगी, सुरक्षित और गरिमापूर्ण जीवन व्यतीत कर सकें । इसका उद्देश्य शैक्षिक, आर्थिक और सामाजिक विकास तथा आवश्यक पुनर्वास के कार्यक्रमों के माध्यम से अपने लक्ष्य समूहों को सहायता प्रदान करना और सशक्त करना है । इस दिशा में भी सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय की कार्य योजनाएं अभूतपूर्व रही हैं । 
  मैं वर्ष 2020-21 के लिए सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय के लिए आवंटित किए गए बजट की अनुदान मांगों का पुरजोर समर्थन करते हुए निवेदन करना चाहूंगा कि गड़चिरोली-चिमुर संसदीय क्षेत्र लगभग 700 किलोमीटर लंबे क्षेत्र में देश का सबसे बड़ा आदिवासी संसदीय क्षेत्र है । यह क्षेत्र अत्‍यधिक पिछड़ा और घना आदिवासी बाहुल्य नक्सल प्रभावित क्षेत्र है । इस आदिवासी क्षेत्र में आदिवासी लोगों के साथ-साथ बंगाली समाज के लगभग 1 लाख से अधिक लोग वर्ष 1962 से पुनर्वास के तौर पर बहुत ही सद्भाव के साथ कई पीढ़ियों से रह रहे हैं । इन में ओबीसी के लोगों की संख्या भी काफी अधिक है । 
  गैर आदिवासी इन सभी लोगों का जीवनयापन जनजातीय लोगों की भांति ही है । ये सभी सामाजिक, आर्थिक एवं शैक्षणिक दृष्टि से बहुत ही पिछड़े हुए हैं । सरकार ने बंगाली समाज के जीवन स्तर में सुधार हेतु मकान आदि की सुविधाएं उपलब्ध कराई हैं, लेकिन आदिवासी क्षेत्र में रहने वाले गैर आदिवासी लोग, जो विगत काफी लंबे अरसे से कब्‍जाई गई भूमि पर खेती करके अपना जीवनयापन कर रहे हैं, को भूमि आवंटन के स्‍थाई पट्टे नियमों की कड़ाई के चलते नहीं मिल पाए हैं, जिस कारण वह सींचन इत्यादि जैसी शासकीय सुविधाओं से वंचित हैं । 
  मेरे आदिवासी संसदीय क्षेत्र में रहने वाले बंगाली और ओबीसी के गरीब गैर आदिवासी लोगों द्वारा विगत काफी समय से यह मांग की जा रही है कि जिस प्रकार से आदिवासी क्षेत्रों में निवास करने वाले आदिवासी लोगों द्वारा जिस भूमि पर खेती की जा रही थी, उस भूमि के पट्टे सरकार ने उनके नाम कर दिए हैं, उसी प्रकार से बंगाली और ओबीसी के गैर आदिवासी लोग, जिनका रहन-सहन जनजातीय लोगों की भांति ही है, को भी उनके द्वारा की जा रही खेती के भूमि के पट्टे को उनके नाम किए जाने संबंधी नियमों में शिथिलता देकर पट्टे उनके नाम कर दिए जाएं तो उनको सींचन इत्यादि जैसी शासकीय सुविधाएं मिलने पर उनके जीवन स्तर में भी सुधार आ सकेगा ।

अतः देश के आदिवासी क्षेत्रों विशेषत: गड़चिरोली-चिमुर आदिवासी संसदीय क्षेत्र में निवास करने वाले बंगाली एवं ओबीसी के लोगों को उनके द्वारा कब्जाई गई भूमि के पट्टे आवंटन करने संबंधी नियमों में शिथिलता प्रदान करके आदिवासियों की भांति उनको भी भूमि के पट्टे दिलाये जाने की आवश्यकता है । 
  नीति आयोग ने देश के 28 राज्यों में 117 जिलों की पहचान आकांक्षी जिलों के रूप में की है, जिसमें नक्सलवाद से पूरी तरह प्रभावित महाराष्ट्र राज्य का आदिवासी बाहुल्य जिला गड़चिरोली भी शामिल है । सरकार द्वारा इन जिलों का शीघ्र और प्रभावी रूपांतरण किए जाने के साथ-साथ इस कार्यक्रम में इस बात पर भी जोर दिया जा रहा है कि विकसित हो रही अर्थव्यवस्था में लोग अपनी भागीदारी कर सकने में पूरी तरह से सक्षम हो । इस कार्यक्रम के अंतर्गत जिन क्षेत्रों पर अधिक बल दिया जा रहा है, उनमें स्वास्थ्य और पोषण, शिक्षा, कृषि तथा जल संसाधन, वित्तीय समावेशन तथा कौशल विकास और बुनियादी अवसंरचना शामिल है । 
  लेकिन नक्‍सलवाद से बुरी तरह प्रभावित आदिवासी बाहुल्य जिला गड़चिरोली, जिसको आकांक्षी जिले के रूप में शामिल किया गया है, में सरकार के इस कार्यक्रम को प्रभावी तरीके से क्रियान्वित नहीं किया जा रहा है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप इस नक्सलवादी आदिवासी बाहुल्य जिले में विकास संबंधी कार्य पूरी तरह से अवरुद्ध है तथा यह पिछड़ा हुआ जिला सरकार की नीति के अनुरूप विकास की ओर अग्रसर नहीं हो रहा है एवं इस जिले में नक्सलवाद की गंभीर समस्या भी ज्यों की त्यों बरकरार है । 
  यदि गड़चिरोली आकांक्षी जिले में सरकार के उपरोक्त कार्यक्रमों का गंभीरता एवं पूर्ण निष्ठा के साथ संचालन किया जाए तो निश्चित रूप से यह आकांक्षी जिला विकास की ओर अग्रसर होगा और यहां पर नक्सलवाद की समस्या का भी निराकरण हो जाएगा । 

अतः आकांक्षी जिले के रूप में गड़चिरोली में केंद्रीय योजनाओं को प्रभावी तरीके से लागू किया जाए । 

अंत में, मैं सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय की अनुदान मांगों का पुरजोर समर्थन करते हुए सरकार को धन्यवाद देता हूं और साथ ही यह भी विनम्र विनती करता हूं कि मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र से संबंधित उपरोक्त सभी मुद्दों पर सहानुभूतिपूर्वक विचार करते हुए उनके निराकरण हेतु धन का आवंटन करने हेतु समुचित कदम उठाने की कृपा करेंगे ।

* SHRI RAJU BISTA (DARJEELING): I wholeheartedly support this budget which is by far the most inclusive budget in the history of our nation. 

This budget has given a definitive push to social sector and increased the budgetary allocation for the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment by 14% and Ministry of Tribal affairs by 7.5%. Allocation of Rs 10,103.57 crore to the Ministry of Social Justice and empowerment for 2020-21 as against the Rs 8,885 crore given to it in 2019-20, shows the commitment of our Government towards ensuring welfare of all the marginalized people across our nation. This budget has fixed Rs 85,000 crore for the welfare of scheduled castes and other backward classes (OBCs), and Rs 53,700 crore for scheduled tribes. In order to eradicate the practice of manual scavenging, this budget has increased pre-matric scholarships for children of workers involved in manual scavenging by 400%. Fellowship for OBCs has been increased by 71.4% and overseas fellowships for OBCs has been increased by 133%

As a youth representative, I am grateful the increased allocation for Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment underpins the three prominent theme based vision that you have presented, outlining the roadmap for our country to move forward in Aspirational India - which seeks to transform the standard of living for our people. Economic Development - which means rethinking our economy with greater private participation, and Caring Society - which is both humane and compassionate. 

The vision that you have presented to us will not only lay strong foundation for the growth of our country, but will also have a lasting impact on the future of our nation.

I represent Darjeeling Lok Sabha constituency. My constituency has one of the highest ratio of SC, ST, OBC and economically backward sections of people. Even though it is one of the most resource rich constituencies, it is also one of the most deprived. Majority of the people here are dependent on working in the tea gardens where they are only paid Rs 176 per day. They don’t have any other source of income. Because of this, many meritorious students from our region, are forced to quit their education, as their parents are unable to afford the cost of education.

All schools of higher learning are situated in the towns like Darjeeling, Siliguri, Kalimpong, Kurseong, Mirik, Bijanbari, Matigara, Bagdogra, Phansidewa. While students come from far-flung rural regions walking to school. There is a place called Jangapana in Kurseong - where from students walk 6 hours each day to reach their school and back. Students from Dhotrey and Miling are forced to leave home at 5 AM in the morning, so that they can reach their school in Ghoom at 9 AM. Imagine the plight of a student, who has to traverse these difficult mountain terrain during high monsoon rain - just to reach their schools. Because of all this, “many students from economically and socially marginalized families have given up their educational dreams. Given this, I request the Hon’ble Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment to kindly construct Hostels for the students from marginalized communities in various town centres like - Darjeeling, Siliguri, Kalimpong, Kurseong, Mirik, Bijanbari, Matigara, Bagdogra, Phansidewa so that they can continue their education and fulfil their dreams. I also request the Hon’ble Minister to kindly allocate additional resources for children from the mountain regions, so that they can find a level playing field in terms of education and career.

I am also hopeful that the Hon’ble Minister Thawarchand Gehlot ji will kindly address these issues confronting Darjeeling hills, Terai and Dooars region, to enable our Youth from socially and economically marginalized families to dream bigger.

*डॉ. वीरेंद्र कुमार (टीकमगढ़):  सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय का कार्य एक समावेशी समाज का निर्माण कर सशक्त बनाना है जिसमें वंचित, पिछड़े लोग अपनी वृद्धि और विकास के लिए पर्याप्‍त समर्थन के साथ उपयोगी, सुरक्षित और सम्मानजनक जीवन जी सकें । इसका लक्ष्य, जहां भी आवश्यक हो, शैक्षिक, आर्थिक और सामाजिक विकास और पुनर्वास के कार्यक्रमों के माध्यम से अपने लक्षित समूहों को सहायता देना और सशक्त बनाना है । 
  सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता विभाग का उद्देश्य अनुसूचित जाति, अन्य पिछड़ा वर्ग, वरिष्ठ नागरिकों, शराब और मादक द्रव्यों के सेवन का शिकार व्यक्तियों, ट्रांसजेंडर व्यक्तियों, भिखारियो, विमुक्त और खानाबदोशों (डीएनटी), आर्थिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्गों (ईबीसी) और, आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्गों (ईडब्ल्यूएस) सहित समाज के सामाजिक, शैक्षिक और आर्थिक रूप से अधिकार हीन वर्ग को सशक्त बनाना है ।
